adversarial_challenges.challenge: Could navigation/deep-link transitions silently replace the saved documentary preference?
adversarial_challenges.finding: NO in the changed controller: persistence requires persist=true AND origin=user; deep-link and temporary-reader calls are explicitly nonpersistent; legacy saved enriched/aflp/additions values remain loadable.

adversarial_challenges.challenge: Could activeReaderSupplement be repurposed and destabilize Reader/session identity?
adversarial_challenges.finding: NO; activeReaderSupplement and sampled reading-position/session persistence functions are byte-identical to v142.10. A separate local documentary resolver was added.

adversarial_challenges.challenge: Could a selection crossing PRINCIPAL/COMPLÉMENT be falsely assigned one source?
adversarial_challenges.finding: NO in targeted tests; mixed selection returns kind=mixed, exact paragraph IDs, and all involved supplement IDs for principal→supplement, supplement→principal and principal→supplement→principal.

adversarial_challenges.challenge: Could stale selection data contaminate provenance after navigation?
adversarial_challenges.finding: Resolver reuses current Reader binding/validity checks; targeted stale-selection case falls through to the current visible paragraph.

adversarial_challenges.challenge: Could scrolling over an internal complement still show host PRINCIPAL provenance?
adversarial_challenges.finding: Resolver prioritizes explicit/valid selection, then explicit paragraph, then top visible paragraph before Reader focus/entry fallback. Infos/source freezes that local target on open.

adversarial_challenges.challenge: Could ordinary UI hide a non-normal documentary view?
adversarial_challenges.finding: All normal Library/Tome/Reader/Search surfaces carry compact status components synchronized from supplementMode; normal HTML contains no permanent data-source-mode selector controls.

adversarial_challenges.challenge: Could Repères OFF erase all documentary distinction?
adversarial_challenges.finding: Internal complement blocks retain background/left-border styling and an accessible group label with Repères OFF; Repères ON exposes the explicit banner/provenance. Complete-entry complement identity remains separately handled.

adversarial_challenges.challenge: Could internal complements inflate ordinary read statistics or date rows show seq:null?
adversarial_challenges.finding: Normal stats only credit principal records plus complete-entry complements; internal supplement records do not add normal-reading entry credit. Date rows use documentary-specific subtitles for supplement records.

adversarial_challenges.challenge: Could this change alter retrieval/corpus/speaker/user schemas?
adversarial_challenges.finding: corpus/**, pls_v15/**, all Search/runtime files, interaction_anchor.js and sampled core persistence/backup functions are byte-identical. Supplement registry/speaker hashes and 75/13/62/177 invariants are unchanged.

adversarial_challenges.challenge: Could release metadata activate stale caches or self-bind to the wrong manifest?
adversarial_challenges.finding: v142.11 has its own worker/shell/runtime identity; offline content binding remains unchanged; version.json offline_manifest_sha256 matches the current manifest.

adversarial_challenges.challenge: Could local automated evidence be mistaken for hosted/PWA/physical proof?
adversarial_challenges.finding: NO claim made. Full fake-origin Chromium navigation is blocked by environment policy (ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR). Hosted App-Test, installed-PWA update/offline, iPhone/iPad and VoiceOver remain OPEN.
